name: momentum_decay_adaptive_v1
author: claude_strategist
mechanism: On NIFTY, large institutional TWAP and VWAP algorithms working directional orders over 5-15 minute windows create positive autocorrelation in 5-second returns — the same institution keeps hitting the bid or ask repeatedly, producing runs of same-sign returns. When the rolling AR(1) coefficient on 5-second returns (over the prior 10 minutes) exceeds ~0.12, it signals an active directional algo is still working its order, and the current 1-minute momentum direction is likely to persist for another 30-90 seconds. We enter in the momentum direction only when AR(1) is positive and confirms persistence, and we widen stops/targets when AR(1) is high (long half-life, slow decay) versus tighter parameters when AR(1) is borderline (fast decay, quick in-out). This rejects mean-reversion bars where AR(1) is near zero or negative.

indicators.name: ar1_120
indicators.purpose: Rolling AR(1) coefficient over 120 bars (10 minutes). Original used 60 1-min bars = 60 minutes of history. At 5s, we compress to 10 minutes because NIFTY momentum regimes (driven by institutional order flow) shift every few minutes — averaging 60 minutes would wash out the very regime signal we need. 120 bars gives enough observations (n~119 pairs) for a statistically meaningful AR(1) estimate (SE ~1/sqrt(119) ~0.09) while remaining sensitive to current conditions.

indicators.name: roc_12
indicators.purpose: 1-minute rate of change in basis points. Direct entry trigger: the prior 60 seconds (12 bars) of directional movement is the immediate momentum signal we are trading for continuation. Original used ROC(10) on 1-min bars = 10 minutes. We compress to 12 bars (1 min) because our hold time is 15-90s — we want to ride the tail of a 60s move, not a 10-min move which would be mostly exhausted by entry time.

indicators.name: vwap_session
indicators.formula: cumsum(close * volume) / cumsum(volume) from session open
indicators.purpose: Session VWAP as directional context filter. No lookback scaling needed — cumulative measure. Ensures we only take CE signals when price is already above VWAP (institutional buy flow dominating benchmark) and PE signals when below. Filters out weak chop signals where price is crossing VWAP repeatedly.

conditions: ar1_120 > ar1_threshold (positive autocorrelation — momentum regime active)
roc_12 > mom_threshold_bps (1-min returns positive, upward momentum)
close > vwap + vwap_filter_bps*vwap/10000 (price above VWAP, buy-side dominant)
buy_ce.confirmation: All three conditions true simultaneously on same 5s bar

conditions: ar1_120 > ar1_threshold (positive autocorrelation — momentum regime active)
close < vwap - vwap_filter_bps*vwap/10000 (price below VWAP, sell-side dominant)
buy_pe.confirmation: All three conditions true simultaneously on same 5s bar

exit.stop_rationale: When ar1_120 is borderline (~0.12), use 3 pts stop — if NIFTY reverses 6 spot pts within 30s the momentum regime read was wrong and we exit immediately. When ar1_120 is strong (~0.35+), use 5-6 pts — high-persistence momentum can temporarily pullback 8-12 spot pts before resuming, so wider stop prevents premature exit on minor retracements.
exit.target_rationale: Strong AR1 momentum on NIFTY (ar1>0.3) carries 20-30 spot pts in 60-120s; 10 pts captures ~50% of that expected move at delta ~0.5. Weak AR1 (borderline) targets 5 pts (~10 spot pts) which is the median 1-min NIFTY move — still 1:1.67 R:R at 3 pt stop.

filters.vix_filter: none — VIX not used; AR1 regime detection self-adapts to volatility
filters.time_filter: 09:30-15:20 IST; skip first 15 minutes to avoid opening auction noise and allow 120-bar AR1 warmup
filters.volume_filter: none direct; VWAP deviation implicitly filters via price-vs-benchmark
filters.trend_filter: AR1 > threshold IS the trend/regime filter — no separate trend filter needed
filters.spread_filter: none — limit order execution, no spread cost

edge.edge_decay_risk: Medium — institutional algo patterns are persistent features of index microstructure, but market structure changes (algo proliferation, NSE rule changes) could erode AR1 predictability

adaptation_notes: Original traded NIFTY50 constituents on 1-min bars, estimating AR1 over 60 minutes. Three key changes: (1) Universe: individual stocks → NIFTY index. Index AR1 reflects institutional program trading more cleanly than individual stocks which have idiosyncratic noise. (2) AR1 window: 60 min → 10 min (120 bars). Regime relevance window at 5s frequency must match the typical institutional order lifespan of 5-15 minutes, not 60 minutes. (3) ROC lookback: 10 min → 1 min (12 bars). Since we hold 15-90s, the trigger must detect momentum that will persist over our hold time — the prior 60s is the right input horizon. Stops and targets are now in option premium points and scale adaptively with AR1 magnitude rather than using FAST/SLOW binary regime.
weaknesses: AR(1) estimated on 120 5-second returns has SE ~0.09 — borderline threshold values (0.10-0.15) will generate noisy regime classifications
NIFTY index returns include dividend adjustments and corporate actions in constituents that create occasional AR1 spikes not related to institutional order flow
Session open (09:15-09:30) is excluded, missing momentum bursts from overnight gap information absorption — but opening auction noise would contaminate AR1 estimates
Adaptive stop/target arrays add implementation complexity; stop/target scale linearly with AR1 which is a simplification of the true half-life → premium move relationship
